13: # Agent Platform Model Tuning
14: 
15: ## Overview
16: 
17: This skill provides procedural knowledge for fine-tuning Large Language Models
18: (both Open Models and Gemini Models) using Agent Platform's tuning service. It
19: covers the entire lifecycle from environment setup and data preparation to job
20: configuration, monitoring, and deployment.

95: ## Phase 0: Environment & IAM Setup {#phase-0}
96: 
97: Ensure the foundational environment is ready before proceeding.
98: 
99: ### 0.1 Authentication & Project Context
100: 
101: -   Check if `gcloud` CLI is installed. If it is not installed, prompt the user
102:     for permission to install it before proceeding. If it is installed, update
103:     it:
104: 
105: ```bash
106: gcloud components update --quiet > /dev/null 2>&1
107: ```
108: 
109: -   Verify `gcloud auth list`. If not authenticated, run `gcloud auth login`.
110: -   Ensure `project` is known. Use `gcloud config get project` to retrieve the
111:     current project.
112: -   **CRITICAL: Ask for Confirmation.** You must prompt the user to confirm the
113:     retrieved project before proceeding, in case they want to switch to a
114:     different one. The location must also be confirmed — see section 0.2 for
115:     which location to propose, which depends on the model category.
116: 
117: ### 0.2 Location
118: 
119: Location handling **depends on the model category** you established in the
120: workflow decision tree. The two categories have different supported locations —
121: never apply one category's locations to the other.
122: 
123: -   **Open models** share one fixed location set, and `global` is the
124:     recommended choice.
125: -   **Gemini models** differ per model and must be looked up. `global` is not
126:     accepted for them today.
127: 
128: If the user names a location that is not valid for their model and category,
129: STOP. Respond with an error naming the requested location as unsupported, list
130: the locations that are valid, and do NOT ask for a dataset, do NOT proceed with
131: any other setup step, and do NOT silently retry elsewhere.
132: 
133: #### Open Models (RECOMMEND: `global`)
134: 
135: **Recommend `global` and confirm it with the user.** Propose it as a single
136: recommended choice rather than making the user pick a region first, and do not
137: steer them toward a specific region instead.
138: 
139: These are the only locations available for open model tuning:
140: 
141: -   `global` (the recommended choice)
142: -   `us-central1`
143: -   `europe-west4`
144: -   `us-west1`
145: -   `us-east5`
146: -   `asia-southeast1`
147: 
148: The `global` endpoint automatically selects a supported region that has
149: available capacity, so it is the most likely to be scheduled successfully.
150: Pinning a region up front restricts the job to that one region's capacity, which
151: is why `global` is the recommended location for open model tuning.
152: 
153: 
154: -   **The user named a location** → use it verbatim, provided it is `global` or
155:     one of the regions listed above. Do not talk them out of it.
156: -   **The user asked which locations are supported** → answer the question.
157:     Share the list above and say that `global` is recommended and why. Never
158:     withhold it.
159: -   **The user did not name a location** → propose `global` and ask them to
160:     confirm it before you proceed. Say that `global` lets the service pick a
161:     region with available capacity. Do NOT silently assume `global`.
162: 
163: The point of proposing a single choice is to avoid making region selection a
164: decision the user must resolve before anything else can happen — that ordering
165: is what previously blocked people. It is not a reason to hide the list: quote it
166: whenever the user asks, and quote it when rejecting an unsupported location.
167: 
168: Fall back to an explicit region **only** in the cases below, and tell the user
169: why you are doing so:
170: 
171: -   **CMEK.** Customer-managed encryption keys are rejected on `global` with a
172:     `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error. A CMEK-protected job must name the region that
173:     holds the key.
174: 
175: -   **Data residency.** If the user requires the job to stay in a specific
176:     jurisdiction, honor their region. `global` currently runs the job in either
177:     `us-central1` or `europe-west4`.
178: 
179: If a `global` job is accepted but then fails with a `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error
180: saying the model does not support global endpoint tuning, that model is not
181: onboarded to the global endpoint yet. The model itself is still tunable:
182: resubmit once in an explicit region from the list above (`us-central1` is the
183: safest choice) and tell the user why you switched.
184: 
185: ##### Working with a `global` job
186: 
187: -   The API host stays `aiplatform.googleapis.com`. There is no
188:     `global-aiplatform.googleapis.com` host.
189: -   The service resolves `global` to a real region at run time. Sub-resources
190:     (the tuned model, checkpoints, TensorBoard) come back with that **real**
191:     region in their resource names, not `global`. Read the location out of the
192:     returned resource name before using it for monitoring or deployment; never
193:     assume it is still `global`.
194: -   Quota is shared across regions, so pinning a region does not grant extra
195:     quota.
196: 
197: #### Gemini Models (per-model, look it up)
198: 
199: `global` is **not accepted for Gemini tuning today** — the service rejects it at
200: job creation with a `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error, so do not propose it here.
201: 
202: 
203: **There is no single region allowlist for Gemini.** Supported tuning regions
204: vary by model and by model version: some Gemini models are restricted to two
205: regions while others support many more. Do NOT reuse the open model list above,
206: and do NOT assume a region carries over from another Gemini model.
207: 
208: Before submitting, look up the chosen model in the supervised fine-tuning
209: documentation and read its **"Supported endpoint for model tuning"**
210: row:
211: [supervised tuning](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/tuning/supervised-tuning)
212: 
213: 
214: -   **The user asked which regions are supported** → look up that specific model
215:     and tell them what the docs say. Do not answer from memory or from the open
216:     model list, and do not answer for a different Gemini model.
217: -   **The model's row names specific regions** → the user's region must be one
218:     of them. If it is not, STOP and report the supported regions for that model.
219: -   **The model's row is absent or the docs are unclear** → ask the user for the
220:     region rather than guessing one.
221: 
222: Confirm the region with the user before proceeding. Note that some Gemini models
223: also restrict CMEK and serve tuned models only on the `us` and `eu` multi-region
224: endpoints, so check the same table for those limits before promising them.
225: 
226: ### 0.3 Enable APIs
227: 
228: Ensure `aiplatform.googleapis.com` and `storage.googleapis.com` are enabled.
229: 
230: ```bash
231: gcloud services enable aiplatform.googleapis.com storage.googleapis.com \
232:     --project=YOUR_PROJECT
233: ```
234: 
235: ### 0.4 IAM Permissions
236: 
237: Verify the following identities have the required roles.
238: 
239: -   **Agent Platform Service Agent**:
240:     `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
241: -   **Managed OSS Fine Tuning Service Agent**:
242:     `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-vertex-moss-ft.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
243: -   **User Identity**: The account running the commands.
244: 
245: ### 0.5 Python Dependencies
246: 
247: The scripts in this skill import `vertexai` (from `google-cloud-aiplatform`),
248: `google-genai`, `google-cloud-storage`, and `datasets`.
249: 
250: **CRITICAL AGENT INSTRUCTION:** Do **not** create a virtual environment, and do
251: not install anything before checking. A venv starts empty and hides packages the
252: environment already provides, forcing a redundant several-minute install.
253: 
254: Probe first and install only if the probe fails:
255: 
256: ```bash
257: python3 -c "import vertexai, google.genai, google.cloud.storage, datasets" \
258:   || pip install -r references/requirements.txt
259: ```
260: 
261: Then run every script with a plain `python3 scripts/...` — no activation prefix.
262: 
263: The `references/requirements.txt` pins are a fallback for an environment that
264: does not already provide these SDKs. Do not apply them on top of a working
265: environment: they would downgrade packages other tools may share.
266: 
267: ## Phase 1: Dataset Preparation & Upload {#phase-1}
268: 
269: ### 1.0 Dataset Discovery & Confirmation

272:     filename or path in their prompt, verify its existence in the workspace
273:     (e.g. via script execution or checking for typos).

312: ### 1.1 Formatting & Validation
313: 
314: -   **Conversion**: If data is in CSV, JSON, or Parquet, use
315:     `scripts/prepare_dataset.py` to convert.
316: -   **Validation Split Confirmation**: If the user only provides a training
317:     dataset, **you must prompt the user** to seek permission to split the
318:     training dataset 90/10 to form a validation dataset (using
319:     `--validation_split 0.1`). If they agree, proceed with the split. If they
320:     decline, just use the training dataset without a validation dataset. Do
321:     **NOT** offer an 80/20 split; the tuning service rejects it, for the reason
322:     given in
323:     [Data Preparation Guide](references/data_prep.md#sizing-the-validation-split).
324: -   **Validation**: If data is already in JSONL, validate it before uploading.
325:     Simply having a `.jsonl` extension is not enough. You must verify that the
326:     content schema is valid for tuning (e.g. correct system/user/model roles).
327: 
328: ```bash
329: python3 scripts/prepare_dataset.py \
330:     --input my_data.jsonl \
331:     --format <messages|messages_gemini> \
332:     --validate_only
333: ```
334: 
335: *(Use `--format messages` for open models and `--format messages_gemini` for
336: Gemini models.)* - Refer to [Data Preparation Guide](references/data_prep.md)
337: for required schemas.
338: 
339: ### 1.2 Upload
340: 
341: Upload formatted `.jsonl` files to GCS using a unique directory (e.g., with a
342: datetime timestamp) to avoid overwriting outputs from different runs.
343: 
344: ```bash
345: ARTIFACTS="gs://YOUR_BUCKET/tuning_agent_job_<datetime>/dataset.jsonl"
346: gcloud storage cp dataset.jsonl "$ARTIFACTS"
347: ```

349: ## Phase 2: Model Configuration & Recommendation {#phase-2}
350: 
351: Help the user choose the best model and parameters. **Always seek user
352: confirmation before submitting the job.**
353: 
354: -   If the user does not specify a specific model in their prompt, calculate
355:     recommendations based on the **Models Catalog**.
356: -   **Prompt for Confirmation:** Present the recommended model to the user and
357:     ask for their confirmation before configuring hyperparameters.
358: 
359: ### 2.1 Configuration
360: 
361: #### For Open Models
362: 
363: -   Recommend `tuning_mode`, `epochs`, `learning_rate`, and `adapter_size` based
364:     on the [Tuning Guide](references/tuning_guide.md) and model-specific
365:     baselines in the [Models Catalog](references/models.md).
366: 
367: #### Verify the Live Model ID
368: 
369: Before submitting the job, run `scripts/list_models.py` and pick `--base_model`
370: only from its `models` output. Do not invent IDs or version numbers.
371: 
372: ```bash
373: python3 scripts/list_models.py --project YOUR_PROJECT --filter gemini
374: ```
375: 
376: Output: `{"models": [...], "total_count": N, "truncated": bool}`.
377: 
378: -   For Gemini, strip `google/` and `@default` (e.g.
379:     `google/gemini-2.5-flash@default` → `gemini-2.5-flash`); for open models,
380:     pass `publisher/family@version` as-is.
381: -   Skip Gemini variants ending in `-embedding`, `-tts`, `-image`,
382:     `-computer-use`, or `-native-audio`; they are not tunable.
383: -   If `truncated` is `true`, re-run with a tighter `--filter` (e.g.
384:     `gemini-2.5`) before deciding the target version is unavailable.
385: -   If `models` is empty, stop and ask the user.
386: 
387: ### 2.2 Calculating Cost (Open Models Only)
388: 
389: -   We can calculate a rough estimate of cost of tuning based on the dataset and
390:     the selected model in the [Models Catalog](references/models.md):
391: 
392:     ```bash
393:     python3 scripts/calculate_cost.py \
394:         --input my_data.jsonl \
395:         --model MODEL_NAME \
396:         --tuning_mode TUNING_MODE \
397:         --epochs epochs
398:     ```
399: 
400:     `--model` takes either the display name (`Qwen 3 8B`) or the same resource
401:     name you pass to `--base_model` (`qwen/qwen3@qwen3-8b`), so the value chosen
402:     in Step 2.1 can be reused as-is.
403:

406: > cannot be found, you **MUST** inform the user that the dataset file does not
407: > exist or cannot be accessed. You **MUST** prompt the user to provide a valid
408: > dataset path, and stop tool execution immediately to wait for their response.
409: > Do **NOT** retry or loop, do **NOT** invent a specific cost number, and do
410: > **NOT** prompt for job submission approval before receiving a valid dataset
411: > from the user.
412: 
413: -   **Prompt for Confirmation:** Present the recommended hyperparameter
414:     configuration and estimated cost to the user and ask for their approval
415:     before proceeding to job submission. Make sure to note that the estimated
416:     cost is just an estimate and can vary from actual billing costs.
